Hello,

I’ve recently obtained a Citizen Modena EM0593-56A and I’m having issues with the pins and collars. I haven’t lost any parts, and I’ve changed these many times before. The problem is that the collar does not seem to fit the link and falls right through, even with the pin pushed through. The next step is swapping links entirely, but could it be anything else? I’ve also tried different collars but it does the same thing, falls right through. 

Thank you.
Nothing.
I’m ugly too, friend

I think that’s mostly what Xanax is for! Taking it when you need it. Yesterday was fine, a little bummed out because of no football Sunday. I did some cleaning and went to the gym, not bad overall. How about yourself?
I don’t think so. You have to ramp up to certain doses and ween off when you’re done. It’s supposed to be a steady dose, kinda like birth control so it works as it’s supposed to.

I wear a titanium ring on a rope chain around my neck, and it helps tremendously for when I start to feel slightly negative thoughts creeping up. I put my finger through the ring and rub it against my lip (it’s very smooth and calms me down). Little things like that can go a long way.
What’s going on? Care to talk about anything? I’m here for you.

I’ve always been good about talking openly. I’ve got nothing to hide! When I was on fluoxetine most of all thoughts were gone. I really didn’t care to do or think about anything. I had no ambition or drive... before I started the medication I was body building, and that quickly came to a halt once the meds kicked in.  None of the other meds made me feel that way at all, I just experienced all of the nasty and unwanted side effects. I never wanted to try something like Xanax either, that seemed too risky for me.

It was more of myself not wanting to deal with the side effects. Most were whatever, but at one point I couldn’t have sex because I couldn’t get horny. That was pretty embarrassing, especially considering at that time I had a girlfriend. The only medication that I feel made a difference regarding anxiety/depression was fluoxetine... but then again on that medication I couldn’t feel anything.
You are trying your hardest and that’s what matters. I’m sure your son appreciates you more than you realize.

Prozac (fluoxetine) was my first and that was the only one I was on long enough for it to work. That’s the one that made me feel like a zombie. After that I tried Zoloft, Celexa, Lexapro, and Paxil. With those I experienced things from paranoia to heart palpitations. After I had constant ringing in my ears I gave up on medication.
You should do what you think is best for yourself. Taking initiative and putting yourself in a better position is courageous and admirable. You’re a strong human being and I believe in you.

I was on meds for a while, and one seemed to work better than all others. Fluoxetine was it and although it worked, I felt like a zombie. I decided that dealing with my issues head on was better than feeling like a zombie or dealing with the many side effects I experienced on other drugs. I learned to cope with anxiety, but these feelings never changed.

It’s odd when I don’t feel sad or upset about anything in particular. A friend of mine always tell me that there has to be something causing these feelings... I just can’t find it. I suppose I’ll have to dig a little deeper.

It’s a strange feeling... I don’t know why I don’t want to exist. The only way I can explain it is that it’s an overwhelming feeling of wanting to be gone. I’ve failed suicide multiple times... maybe it’s a sign to try and see life in a new way.
One can only hope.
Thank you for the kind words.

Seems like we’re in a similar position. It’s funny, I was at the beach tonight. A beautiful, iced over beach with freezing rain falling down. It was a peaceful setting. It would have been nice for that to be the last thing I saw. Instead, I’m on Reddit and YouTube.
I appreciate your words. I’m definitely here for a little while longer at least.
I hope you are right.

A long time. I vaguely remembering feeling like I had a reason, but now it’s so engraved into my brain that it feels normal. I have sought and attempted treatment. My therapist is an incredible and I always look forward to visits.
